extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, administrative-law researchers, and policymakers analyzing federal hearing-examiner caseloads
extracted.subtask_description: Tabular metrics reporting caseload volume, timing, and disposition of proceedings pending before federal hearing examiners across multiple agencies for fiscal years 1957 and 1958. Includes counts by proceeding type, duration buckets, disposition categories, and time-to-decision buckets with interpretive footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending before examiners at beginning of year
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of proceedings pending before examiners at the beginning of the fiscal year (column heading in Table 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 7 note: Figures under '1957' are taken from last year's Table I; discrepancies can arise because agencies differ in what they count as 'proceedings' or due to dormant claims being dropped (e.g., 260 'pony' claims in Indian probate). Some counts may include cases also reported elsewhere; footnotes explain when items are disregarded in over-all computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: New cases assigned to examiners during the fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of new cases assigned to examiners during the fiscal year (column heading in Table 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote: 'The figure given under "New cases" includes cases pending at the beginning of the year. It is not known how many of these cases were assigned to examiners before July 1, 1956.' Agency reporting practices vary; some 'new cases' may be carried forward from prior years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old cases remanded or reassigned during the fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of old cases remanded or reassigned to examiners during the fiscal year (column heading in Table 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts may include consolidated cases or those returned to examiners after agency action; footnotes note inclusion of 'disposed of' by consolidation and other reassignment nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposed of by examiners during the fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of proceedings disposed of by examiners during the fiscal year (column heading in Table 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 9 breaks down 'disposed of by examiners' into manner-of-disposition categories (decision on merits after evidentiary hearing; dismissals/withdrawals; certified to agency upon waiver; default/settlement/compromise/consent; other examiner disposition). Footnotes identify special dispositions (e.g., waivers, consolidations, postponements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending before examiners at end of fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of proceedings pending before examiners at the end of the fiscal year (column heading in Table 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes: Table 7 v. Table I differences arise from reporting changes; Table 8 excludes some proceedings (e.g., Social Security and Indian probate data unavailable for certain tables). Agencies changed definitions and counting techniques between years, causing discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length-of-pending-before-examiners categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of proceedings pending before examiners at end of year by how long they had been before examiners: '3 months or less', 'Over 3 months but not over 6', 'Over 6 months but not over 12', 'Before examiners over 1 year' (Table 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show backlog age. Footnotes explain special counting rules (e.g., CAB safety enforcement 1958 figures reflect time from prehearing conference or opening of hearing rather than assignment date). Some agency practices (e.g., NLRB assignment timing) affect bucket counts; Social Security supplied estimates for longer-duration cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of disposition — Decision on merits after evidentiary hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings disposed of by an examiner via a decision on the merits after an evidentiary hearing (one column in Table 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count of examiner decisions reached after hearing; Table 9 provides per-agency counts. Footnotes note when decisions were waived or cases disposed of by consolidation; comparisons to prior-year tables must account for re-categorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of disposition — Dismissal or withdrawal without decision on merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings dismissed or withdrawn without an examiner decision on the merits (one column in Table 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Column in Table 9 aggregates dismissals and withdrawals (including before and after hearing) and combines several prior-year categories; footnotes explain transfers, withdrawals for agency rulings, and other reasons for removal from examiner jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of disposition — Certified to agency upon waiver of examiner decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings certified to the agency because the examiner's decision was waived (one column in Table 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes cases where the examiner's decision was waived and the matter returned to agency; footnotes indicate that some cases reported as 'other' previously are now in this column when waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of disposition — Default, settlement, compromise or consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings disposed of by default, settlement, compromise, or consent (new column in Table 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This column was added relative to the prior report to capture uncontested dispositions; footnotes warn that some such cases may have been reported previously under 'Other' and may appear differently across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of disposition — Other examiner disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Other methods by which an examiner disposed of proceedings (residual column in Table 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures dispositions not falling into the labeled categories; footnotes give examples (change of venue, escheat, certified to solicitor) and note that some items may be double-counted if transferred between categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total examiner decisions on merits (time-to-decision sample)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of examiner decisions on the merits used as the denominator for time-to-decision analysis (Table 10 heading: 'Total examiner decisions on merits').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 10 restricts analysis to proceedings in which examiners issued decisions on the merits after hearing. Footnotes and agency notes indicate some proceedings/types are excluded or estimated (e.g., Social Security, Indian probate), so totals in Table 10 differ from overall disposed counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time from assignment to examiner to decision buckets
rubrics_metrics.description: Buckets measuring total elapsed time from assignment to examiner to the examiner's decision for merit decisions: 'in 3 months or less', 'Over 3 months but not over 6', 'Over 6 months but not over 12', 'Over 1 year but not over 2', 'Over 2 years' (Table 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess processing speed. Footnotes: variations in start-date definition (e.g., CAB safety enforcement uses prehearing conference/hearing opening instead of assignment); agencies provided estimates for delays (SSA estimated average months for cases beyond 60 days). Differences in bucket counts across years may reflect changes in counting technique or assignment practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of proceedings reported by agencies (proceeding-category taxonomy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency-specific lists of proceeding types reported in the tables (e.g., 'Route licensing' (49 USC §481), 'Stop orders' (15 USC §77h(d)), 'Indian probate' (25 USC §§372,373), NLRB case-types CA/CB/CC/CD/RC etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables break out counts by these proceeding categories for each agency. Footnotes indicate that types were sometimes added or substituted between reports and that some categories were consolidated (e.g., CAB safety enforcement hearing and non-hearing combined in 1957 but separated in 1958). Users should consult footnotes for category changes and cross-year comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting, classification, and comparability caveats (footnotes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretive notes and exceptions governing how counts were tabulated, how categories changed between years, and reasons for discrepancies (extensive footnotes across Tables 7–10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote examples: 1) Table 7 corresponds to prior report's Table I; 2) Types of proceedings were added or substituted; 3) CAB changed measurement start-date for safety enforcement proceedings; 4) Certain cases were disregarded or dropped (e.g., dormant 'pony' claims); 5) Some figures include cases 'disposed of' by consolidation, default, or agreements to discontinue; 6) Social Security and Indian probate data were unavailable for some tables, causing total differences. These notes are essential when comparing year-to-year figures or aggregating across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand totals and agency aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate totals across the 21 reporting agencies (e.g., 'GRAND TOTALS - 21 AGENCIES') shown for various metrics (pending, new, disposed, time buckets, dispositions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation sums agency-level counts but is affected by exclusions and unavailable data (see footnotes noting missing Social Security/Indian probate counts in some tables). The report explains re-categorizations between years and how prior-year figures were used or adjusted.
